editorial.headline: Full National Ownership, Closed Bali Registration for Optical Retail
editorial.standfirst: Though nationally open to full foreign ownership, optical-equipment retail cannot be registered as a PMA activity in Bali under its permanent risk-based moratorium.
editorial.body:
At its centre, this activity is the retail sale of optical equipment and accessories. Its stated examples run from welding goggles and magnifying glasses to monocular and binocular viewing instruments, peepholes, stereoscopes and microscopes. The named examples span protective eyewear, viewing aids and optical instruments, yet they appear in the record as illustrations of one retail scope. The scope also expressly reaches beyond direct sales, although the record gives no further channel-by-channel breakdown.

Who may use the classification is unusually clear on scale. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar businesses, so the record does not limit the activity to a single size of enterprise. Those four labels are each marked open. For a founder, that makes the scale field a practical statement of availability: the stated retail scope is available across every listed business scale, from Mikro through Besar.

At the national level, the foreign-investment position is just as direct. The activity is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In plain English, the national position recorded here permits full foreign ownership of a PMA business carrying this activity. That percentage is national, not a Bali percentage: it belongs to the national PMA field in the record. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. It is a national position, however, and Bali records a materially different registration outcome.

Bali is the decisive exception, with the status BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO. A foreign investor cannot register PMA for this activity in Bali today. At the Besar scale, the OSS risk level is Low or Medium-Low across every stated scope. Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA for all KBLI activities in those Low and Medium-Low risk bands. The stated block is linked to the Bali moratorium dated the thirteenth of May 2026 and identified under Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. The difference is structural: nationally, full foreign ownership is recorded; in Bali, the PMA registration outcome is blocked.
